M1.reason: Outline overlap is 0.95 to 0.96 in all six views (measured), and in the front, back, side, top and below views no part sticks out or is missing. The helmet profile differs slightly (see M3), but the overall outline holds.

M2.reason: Measured size: original 22.8 x 30.2 x 75.3, reproduction 22.7 x 29.9 x 75.1, off by 0.2% to 0.9%, well within 10%.

M3.reason: The helmet is the wrong form. The original's has a clear, rounded visor with a glassy front. The reproduction's is a flat-topped cap with a dark rim and no visible visor (left and right views, angle views). The vest, the gold badge on the chest, the SECURITY lettering on the back and the holster on the right hip are present. The small tab on the upper right of the original's chest and the vest's small parts could not be confirmed as present in the reproduction at this scale.

M4.reason: Colours match by region: violet-blue shirt and trousers, black vest, gold badge, black boots, skin tone. Measured mean colour difference is 6.1 (5.1 to 7.8 by view), under 15. The face and helmet look slightly greyer and more mottled, but within the same colour.

M5.reason: The face is smeared and grainy, and the trousers carry dark blotches in the front and back views, where the original has clean creases. The vest's chest grid and the SECURITY lettering are present but softer than the original's.

M6.reason: At the size the game shows it, the figure reads as the same character, but the grey smeared face, the flat dark helmet and the forward-tipped head make it recognisable as a copy rather than the original.

M7.reason: The front faces forward in the front and back views, the figure stands upright, and both feet sit on the same ground line as the original's (about y 355 in the front view, the same in the side views).

M8.reason: The checks show no errors. The reproduction has 362 triangles against the original's 785, under twice the original's count. Nothing looks open, inside out or floating in the views.

C1.reason: Nothing comes apart in the run frames (RUN2 3/22 to 22/22): the arms, head and holster stay on the body. But the attack does not move as the original's does. The original's shootgun attack leans the torso and head forward with the arm angled down; the reproduction's 2handshoot frames (1/7 to 7/7) stay upright with the arms held straight out level.
